label: Where the server may fetch from: https to public addresses only, every redirect checked

params.name: exceptions
params.label: Purposes allowed past the default (https to a public address only): http true = plain http allowed; nets = private networks it may reach. Link-local / metadata (169.254.x) is never reachable. recite: a speech service on the owner's own computer or LAN; providers: a model served on this computer (Ollama, http://127.0.0.1:11434)

params.name: drop_on_host_change
params.label: Headers dropped when a redirect goes to another host (keys never follow a redirect away)

params.name: direct_pattern
params.label: A line that opens a URL itself (the ratchet's grep)

params.name: direct_files
params.label: Files allowed to open a URL themselves - each only talks to this portal's own local server (launcher, tests, tools)

params.name: direct_ceiling
params.label: Lines in those files that open a URL themselves - only falls

default.scheme: Refused to open {url}: only https addresses may be fetched ({scheme} is not allowed here).
default.host: Refused to open an address on {host}: it is not one this call may reach.
default.address: Refused to open {ip}: a private, local or cloud-metadata address is never fetched from the server.
default.ratchet_file: {file} opens a URL itself ({n} line(s)) - go through core/egress.fetch, or list the file in chip security.egress direct_files if it only talks to its own local server.
default.ratchet_ceiling: {n} lines open a URL outside core/egress.py; the ceiling is {ceiling} (chip security.egress direct_ceiling only falls).

description_nl: 2026-11-18 gap audit C1-17 (server-side request forgery): every outbound fetch - webhooks, AI providers, recite, push, SSO, geo download, funds feed - goes through core/egress.fetch, which refuses non-https, private / loopback / link-local / metadata addresses (checked on the IP actually dialled, again on each redirect) and hosts outside a caller's allow-list. exceptions lets a named purpose use http or a private network (recite: a service on the owner's own computer). direct_files + direct_ceiling: the grep ratchet - only those files may open a URL themselves, and their count only falls. Guard: python -m core.egress.
